name: taking a piss

phase_0.boundary_condition: the urinary tract and pelvic floor musculature

VINIT.justification: the baseline physiological state before the accumulation of urine triggers neural signaling

TANCH.justification: the final state that closes the cycle and returns the system to its resting boundary

AFWD.justification: the directed movement of fluid from the internal reservoir to the external environment

AREV.justification: the reverse force that opposes flow to maintain continence

CLINK.justification: the sequential chaining of bladder wall contraction and sphincter relaxation

IMSCRIB.justification: the conscious recognition of the urge to void as a self-referential signal

FSPLIT.justification: the neural branch point where the system chooses to either initiate flow or maintain storage

FFUSE.justification: the resolution of the voiding decision that returns the system to a singular state of being either empty or full

EVALT.justification: the affirmative execution of the voiding process

EVALF.justification: the failure to initiate flow despite the presence of the urge

ENGAGR.justification: the simultaneous presence of the urge to void and the inability to relax the sphincter

IFIX.justification: the irreversible physiological record of waste removal from the bloodstream

phase_3.void_description: the quiescent state of an empty bladder before filtration begins
phase_3.true_description: the state of active micturition and successful evacuation
phase_3.false_description: the state of continued storage or involuntary retention
phase_3.both_description: the state of paraphysis where the body attempts to void against a closed sphincter

steps.domain_action: the kidneys filter blood to produce urine in the absence of bladder distension
the bladder wall stretches and sends afferent signals to the brain identifying the need to void
the central nervous system evaluates the environmental appropriateness for micturition
the brain signals the external sphincter to relax and the detrusor muscle to contract
urine moves through the urethra toward the exit point
the volume of urine is permanently removed from the internal biological system
the bladder reaches a state of collapse and the flow ceases
the sphincter muscles re-engage to seal the urinary tract
the detrusor muscle relaxes to allow for the next cycle of accumulation
the system returns to the baseline state of a closed and empty vessel

phase_5.memory_mechanism: the distension threshold of the bladder wall
phase_5.alfs_store: the homeostatic set points for fluid and electrolyte balance

phase_6.pre_cycle_state: high potential energy in a distended bladder
phase_6.post_cycle_state: low potential energy in a collapsed bladder
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the energy consumed in the mechanical release is balanced by the restoration of homeostatic equilibrium
